task: Align Dockerfile builder to Go 1.26, pin the full apk closure in both stages, and gate the Dockerfile build in CI before release (#26)

events.summary: Scoped to the Dockerfile (builder FROM line, both apk add lines), a new image-build job in .github/workflows/ci.yaml, and this trace file. go.mod (go 1.26.0), ci.yaml's existing go-version/go-version-input pins, the chart's appVersion, release.yaml, and application code were confirmed already correct or out of scope and left untouched. A second-opinion supply-chain review of the first pass requested two corrections, both applied: (1) pin the full transitive closure apk installs in each stage, not just the named top-level packages; (2) add a CI job that builds the Dockerfile for every release.yaml platform before a release tag is pushed, since no existing job did. Both were implemented and verified below, including on linux/arm/v7 which had not been exercised for this Dockerfile before.

Directly observed the three problems this change fixes. (1) Toolchain drift: the Dockerfile builder was golang:1.27-alpine while go.mod declared `go 1.26.0` and every go-version/go-version-input pin in .github/workflows/ci.yaml was already '1.26' -- read directly from all three files, a real and verifiable inconsistency, not a hypothetical one. (2) Non-reproducible apk installs: the runtime and builder apk add lines named only the top-level packages (xfsprogs-extra, quota-tools, e2fsprogs, util-linux, btrfs-progs; git in the builder), while the digest-pinned base images left every transitive dependency -- 60 additional runtime packages, 11 additional builder packages -- resolving from the still-mutable Alpine 3.24 apk index on each rebuild; confirmed by extracting P:/V: pairs from /lib/apk/db/installed in the bare digest-pinned base images (alpine:3.24@sha256:28bd5f..., golang:1.26-alpine@sha256:b6890e...) and diffing against the same file in images built with only the five/one named packages installed -- 65 and 12 packages respectively existed in the built image but not the bare base, none of them version-pinned. (3) No pre-release build gate: neither ci.yaml nor release.yaml ran `docker build` anywhere before release.yaml's build-and-push job, which only runs on a pushed release tag -- confirmed by reading both workflow files -- so a dependabot digest bump landing on an Alpine point release that dropped one of these pins would stay green through every existing CI job and fail only after the tag was already pushed.

Fixed all three. (1) Builder FROM changed from golang:1.27-alpine@sha256:4c9fe601... to golang:1.26-alpine@sha256:b6890e35ded5d19118c2bca3d7754dc4e6f694aac2d0aeb92f9807c2879e4230, the multi-arch manifest-list digest (covers linux/amd64, arm64, arm/v6, arm/v7, 386, ppc64le, riscv64, s390x; resolves to Go 1.26.8 on alpine3.24), resolved via `docker buildx imagetools inspect golang:1.26-alpine` on 2026-09-02. (2) Both apk add lines now pin the full closure computed as (packages in the built image) minus (packages in the bare digest-pinned base), one `name=version-release` per line, sorted: 65 lines on the runtime stage (xfsprogs-extra, quota-tools, e2fsprogs, util-linux, btrfs-progs and every package apk pulled in for them, e.g. libuuid, python3, linux-pam), 12 on the builder stage (git and its closure, e.g. libcurl, libidn2, nghttp2-libs). Comments above each RUN line say this pins 'the full closure of packages this stage adds', that the base digest already freezes everything else, and that a pin vanishing from the Alpine 3.24 index fails the build loudly rather than drifting silently. (3) Added an `image-build` ("Image Build") job to ci.yaml that runs on every push/PR: docker/setup-qemu-action + docker/setup-buildx-action + docker/build-push-action build the Dockerfile for linux/amd64, linux/arm64 and linux/arm/v7 (the same three platforms release.yaml's build-and-push job targets) with push:false, load:false, cache-from/cache-to type=gha; every action pinned to the exact commit SHA release.yaml already uses for it. harden-runner runs in egress-policy:block with an allowlist assembled from the job's known fetches (GitHub, Docker Hub registry/auth endpoints, dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org, the Go module proxy/sumdb/GCS backing store), documented in a comment above the allowlist in the same style as the License Check job's, and the job is mentioned in the top-of-file egress-policy inventory comment.

The Dockerfile builder had drifted one Go minor version ahead of go.mod and every CI go-version pin, and apk installs in both stages were not reproducible: of the 77 packages apk actually installed across the two stages (65 runtime + 12 builder), none were version-pinned before this change, so they resolved from a live, mutable index on every rebuild despite the base image itself being digest-pinned. Fixed by realigning the builder digest to golang:1.26-alpine (1.26.8-alpine3.24) and pinning every package in the closure apk actually installs in each stage -- computed via `apk info -v` / `/lib/apk/db/installed` diffed against each stage's bare base image, not guessed -- plus adding the image-build CI job so a future base-digest bump that drops one of these pins from the Alpine index is caught on the next PR instead of after a release tag is pushed.

docker build --no-cache -t nfs-quota-agent:toolchain-check2 . succeeded end to end with the full 65+12-package closure pinned. The resulting image's /lib/apk/db/installed P:/V: package set (81 packages, runtime stage) was byte-for-byte identical to the pre-closure-pin build's package set, confirming every one of the 65 runtime pins resolved to the exact expected version with none dropped, substituted, or left to float; the builder stage's 12 pins installed cleanly with matching version numbers in the build log. `docker run --rm --entrypoint apk nfs-quota-agent:toolchain-check info -v` still lists btrfs-progs-6.17.1-r1, e2fsprogs-1.47.4-r0, quota-tools-4.11-r0, util-linux-2.42.1-r0 and xfsprogs-extra-7.0.1-r0. `docker run --rm --entrypoint /nfs-quota-agent nfs-quota-agent:toolchain-check version` printed 'nfs-quota-agent version dev'. `docker run --rm --entrypoint go nfs-quota-agent:builder-check version` printed 'go version go1.26.8 linux/arm64'. `python3 scripts/ci/check-mutable-inputs.py .github/workflows/ci.yaml .github/workflows/release.yaml .github/workflows/agent-behavior.yml` printed 'Mutable-input guard passed for 3 file(s)', confirming the new image-build job's actions are all pinned to 40-char commit SHAs with no :latest tag. `make test` passed with zero FAIL lines across all packages.
events.scope: Dockerfile full-closure pin reproducibility, binary startup, builder toolchain version, and CI workflow static validation (action pinning) on the colima docker context (aarch64); does not exercise quota enforcement, which this change does not touch

events.summary: Verified the closure-pinned Dockerfile and the new CI job's target platform set work on linux/arm/v7, previously unexercised for this Dockerfile and not natively supported by the colima buildx builder (which only listed linux/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/amd64/v2, linux/386). Installed QEMU emulation with `docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install all`, which added linux/arm/v7 (and v6) to the supported platform list. `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm/v7 --no-cache -t nfs-quota-agent:armv7-check --load .` then succeeded end to end, including the Go build step running under QEMU emulation and all 65 runtime apk pins installing without a single version-resolution error. `docker run --platform linux/arm/v7 --rm --entrypoint apk nfs-quota-agent:armv7-check info -v` showed btrfs-progs-6.17.1-r1, e2fsprogs-1.47.4-r0, quota-tools-4.11-r0, util-linux-2.42.1-r0 and xfsprogs-extra-7.0.1-r0 -- the identical pinned versions seen on amd64/arm64, confirming the pins are not architecture-specific and the same Alpine index resolution holds across arches. Separately confirmed via the Docker Hub registry API (bearer token obtained from auth.docker.io, manifest fetched from registry-1.docker.io with an OCI image-index Accept header) that the golang:1.26-alpine manifest list includes a linux/arm/v7 platform entry alongside amd64, arm64, arm/v6, 386, ppc64le, riscv64 and s390x, so the new builder base itself supports the third platform the new image-build CI job and release.yaml both target.
events.scope: arm/v7 build correctness and apk pin version parity under QEMU emulation on the colima docker context, plus the golang:1.26-alpine base image's platform coverage confirmed independently via the Docker Hub registry API

events.summary: #26's supply-chain-hardening scope, including both corrections from the second-opinion review, is done within the scope stated in e1 and at the evidence level in e5 and e6: the Dockerfile builder matches go.mod and CI at Go 1.26 via a multi-arch manifest-list digest; every apk-installed package in the full closure of both stages (65 runtime, 12 builder) is pinned to the exact version the digest-pinned bases resolved on 2026-09-02, verified reproducible and identical across amd64, arm64 and arm/v7; and a new CI job builds the Dockerfile for all three release platforms on every PR so a future base-digest bump that drops one of these pins is caught before a release tag is pushed, not after.
Complete at the build, full-closure-pin-reproducibility, arm/v7-parity, CI-static-validation and unrelated-test-suite level; nothing outstanding was deferred.
